standards: WHATWG URL Standard (basic URL parser, host, IPv4/IPv6, percent-encode sets, origin, serialisation)
UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing, Unicode 18.0.0 IdnaMappingTable
RFC 5893 Bidi rule and RFC 5892 ContextJ
licence_note: Unicode data files are used under the Unicode License v3; the web-platform-tests data is BSD-3-Clause (Copyright web-platform-tests contributors). No url, idna or ICU code or data was copied: parser, tables and algorithms were written from the standards.

tables.generator: One-off Python (source below) over IdnaMappingTable.txt, UnicodeData.txt, DerivedNormalizationProps.txt, DerivedBidiClass.txt and DerivedJoiningType.txt of Unicode 18.0.0, written as little-endian u32 words.

conformance_data.result: 896 cases: 754 match the expected components exactly (including rejections), 135 are file URLs refused outright, 7 are lenient-Punycode hosts rejected on purpose

deviations_from_the_standard.behaviour: refused with ParseError::UnsupportedScheme; ECDEV never reads files and redirect policy maps the refusal to PUBLIC_HTTP_URL_REQUIRED

deviations_from_the_standard.what: lenient Punycode (IgnoreInvalidPunycode in the newest standard revision)
deviations_from_the_standard.behaviour: seven WPT hosts (xn--pokxncvks under three spellings, 10.0.0.xn--pokxncvks under three spellings, https://xn--/) are rejected, as the url crate rejected them; rejecting is the safe side for a fetcher

deviations_from_the_url_crate_it_replace.behaviour: percent-encoded as %5E, as the standard and WPT require; the url crate left it literal

deviations_from_the_url_crate_it_replace.what: three or more slashes after a special base ('///host')
deviations_from_the_url_crate_it_replace.behaviour: resolved as the standard says; redirect_target now refuses any Location starting '///' explicitly so the redirect policy does not depend on the parser
failure, as the standard says; the url crate accepted
an ordinary character, as the standard says; the url crate treated it as a slash
tables are Unicode 18.0.0; the url crate's are Unicode 16, so a host containing one of the 17810 code points assigned since is accepted natively where the url crate rejected it

differential_proof.oracle: url 2.5.8 (idna 1.1.0, Unicode 16) Url::parse, join, set_*, query_pairs_mut, path_segments_mut
differential_proof.corpus: domain/commerce/tests/web_address_corpus (deterministic): 1.2 million generated absolute and relative references, 600000 random international hosts, 2800+ mutator scripts
differential_proof.disagreements: none outside the documented differences; the first runs found and fixed: a leading Punycode delimiter, '+' accepted by from_str_radix in IPv4 numbers, set_path with an empty path, the query_pairs_mut empty-query form, and path_segments_mut ignoring '.' and '..'

closure: the url crate is no longer a dependency of any ECDEV crate; it remains in Cargo.lock only through reqwest until the HTTP client is replaced
